summary: The Independent reports that viewers consider Princess Diana's final phone call with her sons, shown in episode three of The Crown season six, the series' most heartbreaking scene. In it, Diana tells William and Harry she is not marrying Dodi Fayed and will see them the next night, though she dies that evening. The article also covers the season's release schedule, the crash depiction, and Elizabeth Debicki's comments on filming it.
one_line: Fans on social media call Princess Diana's last phone call with William and Harry in The Crown season six the show's most heartbreaking scene.
key_facts: Netflix released the first four episodes of The Crown's final season (season six) on 16 November, with the last six episodes following on 14 December.
Season six is set between the late 1990s and mid-2000s and includes the lead-up to Princess Diana's fatal Paris car crash in 1997.
Elizabeth Debicki plays Diana, Rufus Kampa plays Prince William, Fflyn Edwards plays Prince Harry, and Khalid Abdalla plays Dodi Fayed.
In episode three, paparazzi delay Diana's scheduled phone call with William and Harry until later that evening.
In the scene, William (then 15) and Harry (then 12) ask when she is coming home, and Diana replies: "I'm coming home tomorrow, and I'm seeing you both tomorrow night."
Diana tells William: "I'm emphatically not going to marry Dodi. To be honest, I can't wait to come home."
Diana says: "Mummy just needs to make some changes to her life, that's all. But that's not your problem, that's mine."
Diana and Dodi, along with chauffeur Henri Paul, were killed on 31 August 1997 when their Mercedes-Benz, pursued by paparazzi, crashed in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris; Diana was 36.
The crash is recreated in the very first scene of season six but is not shown on-screen; a car is seen speeding past a man walking his dog before entering the tunnel.
Fans on X, formerly Twitter, said the call "broke my heart" and was "heartbreaking".
Elizabeth Debicki, an Australian actor, took over the role of Diana from Emma Corrin in season five.
Debicki told Netflix the paparazzi scene was "heavy and very manic, and incredibly invasive" and "difficult to recreate".
